dimensions.note: one row per value in range; formula assumes range resolves to a NumericRange-family object with numberOfSteps - a bare Range's step count is len(range.values) instead

one column per entry of outputVariableMap, or just the range-values column alone if outputVariableMap is empty; a column whose subTask output is itself multi-dimensional would add further dimensions beyond this, not captured here

each entry collapses the range dimension of [id] to a single value (per Repeat, the applied dimension defaults to this Scatter's own range), unless the underlying subTask output was itself multi-dimensional, in which case that dimensionality carries through per entry

[id].range.note: the current value of range, within each iteration

[id].index.note: the current index into range, within each iteration
